narrativeReportMd:
# MarketingStatus R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard R4-to-R6 instance-breaking change was found for local `MarketingStatus`: the R6 datatype keeps the same local element names and types, and R4 instances that include the formerly mandatory fields remain structurally representable. The material local risks are in the opposite direction and in runtime assumptions: R6 makes `country` and `dateRange` optional, so valid R6 content can fail R4 validation or break generated/business code that assumed those elements were always present.

## Scope
The report covers the core `MarketingStatus` datatype only. It excludes inherited base hierarchy changes (`BackboneElement` to `BackboneType`/`DataType`) and inherited extension behavior, which should be owned by the base datatype reports.

## Main migration themes
The main theme is relaxed requiredness. `MarketingStatus.country` and `MarketingStatus.dateRange` move from `1..1` in R4 to `0..1` in R6. This is permissive for R4-to-R6 validation but creates R6-to-R4 representability gaps and nullable-field/codegen churn. The second theme is semantic generalization from medicinal product/marketing authorization wording to more generic item-level marketing status wording, with less explicit ISO 3166 and ISO/TS 20443 guidance in the datatype text.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `MarketingStatus.country` and `MarketingStatus.dateRange` becoming optional. Neither invalidates complete R4 instances in R6, but both can make R6-valid fragments impossible to down-convert to valid R4 without deriving or inventing regulatory data.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is recommended where R6 data omits country or date range, because a safe transform depends on regulatory context. Human review is also useful for the broadened wording to decide whether implementation-specific profiles must preserve the older medicinal-product constraints.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The cardinality relaxations are probably intentional for a broader R6 datatype, but they could have been less disruptive for bidirectional exchange if the base datatype had preserved R4 requiredness and relaxed it only through profiles or a new specialized structure. That alternative would have preserved R4 round-trip guarantees at the cost of less flexibility in R6.

## Follow-up analysis
Base datatype reports should analyze the `BackboneElement`/`BackboneType`/`DataType` hierarchy shift and inherited extension-constraint changes. Resource-specific reports should analyze changed usages of `MarketingStatus` in medicinal product, packaged product, and manufactured item resources.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MarketingStatus` has no local hard R4-to-R6 validation break, but it has two high R6-to-R4 representability risks: R6 can omit `country` and `dateRange`, both mandatory in R4. Runtime/codegen impact is mainly nullable-field churn and business rules that assumed those values were present. The main uncertainty is whether full specification narrative or external profiles impose additional terminology or conformance expectations not visible in the core StructureDefinitions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat R4-to-R6 as mostly permissive for this datatype, while treating R6-to-R4 conversion as lossy unless `country` and `dateRange` can be recovered from context. Generated model updates should account for `country` and `dateRange` becoming optional in R6. Domain teams should review whether the R6 generalization from medicinal product to item changes local regulatory semantics.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas because both local StructureDefinitions are present and directly comparable. Confidence is medium for semantic impact because the computable definitions show wording changes, but no official diff, ballot rationale, or full narrative pages were supplied. Terminology confidence is high that there are no local binding-strength or value-set changes in this datatype, because neither R4 nor R6 declares local bindings on the analyzed elements.

findings.title: MarketingStatus.country changed from mandatory to optional

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a `MarketingStatus` instance was required to include exactly one `country` element.

constraints.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

semanticText.short: The country in which the marketing status applies
semanticText.definition: The country in which the marketing status applies.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `country` may be omitted while the remaining `MarketingStatus` content can still be valid.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard R4-to-R6 validation break because an R4-valid instance already has `country`, and R6 still accepts it. It is a high R6-to-R4 representability risk because an R6-valid `MarketingStatus` can omit `country`, while R4 requires it. Runtime risk is medium for generated models, validators, and business rules that previously treated `country` as non-null.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Country is central to interpreting marketing status in a regulatory context. Inventing or dropping it during backward conversion can change the jurisdictional meaning of availability.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow MarketingStatus to describe broader item-level availability where a country is not always known, applicable, or mandatory.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: lowering `country` from `1..1` to `0..1` preserves R4-valid MarketingStatus instances because R4 required `country` and R6 still permits it.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of allowing broader item-level marketing status when country is unknown, inapplicable, or supplied elsewhere is reasonable. This change does not make old R4 instances invalid in R6; the compatibility cost is primarily reverse conversion and runtime assumptions that `country` is always present.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible base alternative is needed for this finding. Existing R4 data with `country` remains valid under R6. Requiring `country` in R6, or recovering it through profiles, conversion rules, or data-absent policies, would improve R6-to-R4 round-tripping but would be a stricter design or migration mitigation, not a less-breaking base R6 alternative for preserving R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is nullable-field handling and R6-to-R4 conversion gaps; keeping `country` mandatory would restrict the intended R6 flexibility rather than avoid an R4-to-R6 instance break.

evidence.detail: R4 `MarketingStatus.country` has cardinality 1..1 and type CodeableConcept.
R6 `MarketingStatus.country` has cardinality 0..1 and type CodeableConcept.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is illustrative rather than a complete containing resource. It shows an R6-valid `MarketingStatus` shape with `status` and `dateRange` but no `country`; the same fragment cannot satisfy R4 `MarketingStatus.country` minimum cardinality without adding country information.

findings.narrativeMd: `MarketingStatus.country` is the clearest local cross-version compatibility issue: R4 required it, while R6 permits it to be absent. This does not reject old R4 data in R6, but it changes the contract for consumers. Code generated from R6 must allow a missing country, and any system converting R6 content back to R4 must either recover country from context or fail/flag the record.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is permissive for this element: an R4-valid instance with `country` remains valid with respect to `country` in R6. R6-to-R4 is not lossless: an R6 instance that omits `country` is valid under the R6 datatype but violates R4 minimum cardinality. Strict generated R4 classes, JSON-schema-like validators, and FHIRPath/business rules assuming `country.exists()` will be affected.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, no transform is required for `country` beyond normal version conversion. For R6-to-R4 conversion, do not invent a country silently. Try to derive it from the containing resource, authorization context, jurisdictional metadata, or implementation profile; if unavailable, flag for manual review or use an agreed data-absent policy/profile. Test converters with present-country, missing-country, and context-derived-country cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably intentional because R6 generalizes `MarketingStatus` beyond the older medicinal-product authorization wording. A backward-compatible alternative for bidirectional exchange would have kept the base element mandatory and introduced a profile or specialized structure for cases where country is unavailable. That alternative would protect R4 validators but make the R6 core datatype less flexible.

semanticText.definition: The dates that the item is made available on the market by the owner (or where applicable, the manufacturer/distributor) in a country and/or jurisdiction. Note that "on the market" refers to the release of the item into the distribution chain.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `dateRange` may be omitted while the remaining `MarketingStatus` content can still be valid.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard R4-to-R6 validation break because an R4-valid instance already has `dateRange`, and R6 still accepts it. It is a high R6-to-R4 representability risk because R6 permits MarketingStatus without an availability period, while R4 requires one. Runtime risk is medium for generated classes and business logic that assumed a non-null Period.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The availability period is often operationally important for determining whether an item is on market, suspended, or restored. Dropping or fabricating it can affect regulatory and supply-chain interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow MarketingStatus records where market availability dates are unknown, inapplicable, or not yet determined.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: lowering `dateRange` from `1..1` to `0..1` preserves R4-valid MarketingStatus instances because R4 required `dateRange` and R6 still accepts it.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 wording supports a reasonable goal of representing marketing status even when precise market-availability dates are unknown, inapplicable, or not yet determined. The change is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break, but it does create reverse-conversion and runtime-nullability risks.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible base alternative applies. R4 instances already contain `dateRange` and remain valid in R6. A stricter R6 base cardinality, profile requirement, extension policy, or converter backfill rule may help systems that must export to R4, but those are reverse-conversion or local-conformance strategies rather than a less-breaking base R6 design for R4 instance preservation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is nullable Period handling and lossy R6-to-R4 conversion when dates are omitted; retaining base mandatory cardinality would block the intended R6 unknown-date cases.

evidence.detail: R4 `MarketingStatus.dateRange` has cardinality 1..1 and type Period.
R6 `MarketingStatus.dateRange` has cardinality 0..1 and type Period.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is illustrative rather than a complete containing resource. It shows an R6-valid `MarketingStatus` shape with `country` and `status` but no `dateRange`; the same fragment cannot satisfy R4 `MarketingStatus.dateRange` minimum cardinality without adding a Period.

findings.narrativeMd: `MarketingStatus.dateRange` changes from required to optional. The validation direction is easy to miss: R4 data is not made invalid by R6, but R6 data can now omit a Period that R4 required. Implementers that generated non-null Period properties or assumed date availability in downstream logic must handle absence explicitly.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is permissive for this element. R6-to-R4 conversion is potentially lossy or invalid when `dateRange` is absent, because R4 requires a `Period`. Strict R4 validators and generated classes will reject or fail on an omitted `dateRange` unless a conversion policy supplies one.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6 migration, preserve the existing `dateRange`. For R6-to-R4 conversion, derive the period from source system history, regulatory authorization dates, or containing-resource context where possible. If unavailable, flag for manual review rather than silently using a placeholder. Test converters with complete Periods, missing Periods, and partially populated Periods.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably justified if R6 needs to represent status when precise market dates are unavailable. A less disruptive alternative would have preserved mandatory `dateRange` in the base datatype and used profiles/extensions for unknown-date cases. That alternative is better for R4 compatibility but less expressive for incomplete R6 records.

findings.title: MarketingStatus wording was generalized and several R4 conformance cues were removed

oldState.summary: R4 text framed the datatype around medicinal product marketing authorization and included stronger conformance cues for country and market-date details.

semanticText.definition: The marketing status describes the date when a medicinal product is actually put on the market or the date as of which it is no longer available.
semanticText.comment: Local element text referenced marketing authorisation, Medicines Regulatory Agency terminology, ISO 3166 alpha-2 country coding, ISO/TS 20443 status information, and complete ISO 8601 dates for dateRange/restoreDate.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 describes `MarketingStatus` primarily in medicinal-product authorization terms. Several element definitions use `shall` language or cite external standards, although those details are not represented as computable bindings or invariants in the core datatype.

newState.summary: R6 text describes a more generic item-level marketing status and simplifies or removes several explicit R4 conformance cues.

semanticText.definition: The marketing status describes the date when an item is actually put on the market or the date as of which it is no longer available.
semanticText.comment: R6 local element text uses generic item wording, shorter country/jurisdiction/status descriptions, a broader dateRange description, and a clarified restoreDate definition for return after suspension.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 generalizes the datatype from medicinal products to items and shortens the local definitions. This aligns with broader use in R6 resources, but may weaken assumptions that R4 implementers derived from the descriptive text.

facts.oldValue: The marketing status describes the date when a medicinal product is actually put on the market or the date as of which it is no longer available.
facts.newValue: The marketing status describes the date when an item is actually put on the market or the date as of which it is no longer available.

facts.oldValue: Country where the marketing authorisation has been granted; should use ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code elements.
facts.newValue: The country in which the marketing status applies.

facts.oldValue: Marketing status of the medicinal product, with R4 text referring to ISO/TS 20443.
R4 restoreDate reused the placed-on-market/dateRange wording.
facts.newValue: R6 restoreDate is the date the item is due to be placed back on the market after a suspension.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are not direct machine-validation breaks because the relevant R4 wording was not encoded as bindings, fixed values, value limits, or additional invariants in the core datatype. They are still a semantic/conformance risk: implementations may have treated the R4 text as requiring medicinal-product authorization context, ISO country coding, ISO/TS 20443-aligned status values, or complete dates. R6's broader wording may admit valid content whose business meaning is not equivalent to R4 expectations.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Marketing status can drive regulatory availability and supply-chain decisions. A broader or less constrained interpretation may be safe only if local profiles preserve the jurisdiction and status semantics required by the implementation.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize the datatype so it can be reused for item-level marketing status outside the narrower R4 medicinal-product wording and clarify restoreDate.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the wording generalization preserves the R4 element names, datatypes, and R4-valid content shape; it is semantic guidance, not an R4-to-R6 base validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing MarketingStatus from medicinal-product wording to item-level wording is a reasonable R6 goal, and the removed R4 cues were not expressed as computable bindings, invariants, or value limits in the base datatype. The change can still surprise implementations that treated the R4 narrative as policy, but the level of base instance breakage is low.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A clearer transitional narrative could have mentioned medicinal-product regulatory use, ISO 3166 country coding, or ISO/TS 20443 status guidance while introducing the broader R6 item language. That would reduce semantic surprise, but it would be explanatory guidance or profile-level policy rather than a base-design alternative needed to keep R4-valid instances valid in R6; carrying the old wording as hard base guidance could also conflict with generalized non-medicinal item use.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining medicinal-product and ISO cues in comments or profiles could ease transition, but that is guidance or local conformance policy and may overconstrain the broader item-level R6 scope.

evidence.detail: R4 root definition refers to a medicinal product.
evidence.quote: The marketing status describes the date when a medicinal product is actually put on the market...

evidence.detail: R6 root definition refers to an item.
evidence.quote: The marketing status describes the date when an item is actually put on the market...

evidence.detail: R4 country text says the marketing authorization country shall be specified and refers to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code elements.
R6 country text is shortened to the country where the marketing status applies.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON instance example is included because the change is semantic text, not a distinct JSON shape beyond the cardinality relaxations covered in the other findings.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes the local meaning from a medicinal-product authorization-oriented datatype to a more generic item marketing-status datatype. It also simplifies several element definitions, removing explicit R4 cues such as ISO 3166 country-code wording, ISO/TS 20443 status reference, and `shall be provided` date wording. Because those cues were not encoded as core bindings or invariants, this is primarily a semantic/conformance and implementation-policy risk rather than a direct validator failure.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Core validation will not detect most of this semantic shift: both versions keep the same element names and datatypes, and no local value-set binding changed. R4 instances remain structurally acceptable in R6 if they satisfy the unchanged datatypes. R6 instances can be semantically broader than R4 expectations, especially when profiles or business rules expected medicinal-product authorization context or specific country/status coding conventions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review local profiles, validators, and business rules that used R4 text as normative guidance. If an implementation still needs medicinal-product-only semantics, ISO country coding, or specific marketing-status vocabularies, express those requirements in R6 profiles or implementation guides rather than relying on the base datatype text. For R6-to-R4 conversion, flag generalized item statuses for domain review if they do not clearly correspond to an R4 medicinal-product marketing status.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader wording may be justified by expanded reuse of the datatype in R6, but the same goal could have been achieved with explicit transitional notes or profiles preserving R4 regulatory guidance. That would reduce surprise for implementers but would make the base narrative longer and might imply constraints the R6 core no longer wants to impose.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding is intentionally not counted as a hard validation break. Its impact depends on how strongly implementers treated R4 narrative text as conformance policy in the absence of computable bindings.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, and derivation are unchanged. Status/maturity and baseDefinition changed, but those are treated as non-breaking maturity metadata or inherited/base-artifact scope rather than local identity loss.
The same local differential element ids are present in both versions: `country`, `jurisdiction`, `status`, `dateRange`, and `restoreDate`. No local element was removed, renamed, split, or moved.
Local element datatypes are unchanged: `country`, `jurisdiction`, and `status` remain `CodeableConcept`; `dateRange` remains `Period`; `restoreDate` remains `dateTime`.
`MarketingStatus` has no local `Reference`-typed elements in either version.
No local terminology binding is declared on the analyzed `MarketingStatus` elements in either R4 or R6, so there is no local binding-strength or value-set delta.

The local business elements continue to carry only the inherited `ele-1` constraint. Differences on inherited `extension`/`modifierExtension` constraints, such as `ext-1`, are excluded as base/extension-scope changes.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value was found in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were found in either version.
The local business elements remain non-modifier. The inherited `modifierExtension` modifier flag is a base-artifact concern and is unchanged in the inspected snapshots.
The local business elements remain summary elements in both versions.
No local MarketingStatus-specific slicing was introduced or removed. Inherited extension slicing is excluded from local findings.

No local element rename, choice-type change, type replacement, or representation change alters JSON/XML property names for the local business elements. Optionality-driven code generation risk is captured in the cardinality findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status and standards status increased
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 `MarketingStatus` is `status=draft` with standards-status `draft`; R6 is `status=active` with standards-status `normative`. This is maturity metadata and does not by itself invalidate instances or change JSON/XML shape.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may treat normative R6 content as more stable, but should remember this package is an R6 ballot build.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds a FiveWs mapping and world jurisdiction metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 StructureDefinition adds W5 mapping metadata and a jurisdiction entry for World. These do not change local element validation, cardinality, or serialization.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Mapping-aware tooling may expose `MarketingStatus` differently in R6, but instance data does not require a transform for this metadata.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Same canonical datatype identity retained
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 counterpart retains `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/MarketingStatus`, id/name/type `MarketingStatus`, kind `complex-type`, abstract `false`, and derivation `specialization`. There is no local rename, split, or merge to resolve.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Version-aware tooling should still distinguish R4 and R6 by package/FHIR version because the cardinalities and definitions changed.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `MarketingStatus` changes baseDefinition from R4 `BackboneElement` to R6 `BackboneType`, which itself specializes `DataType`. Under the inherited/base-artifact scope rule, superclass hierarchy and inherited `id`/`extension`/`modifierExtension` behavior should be assessed in the base datatype reports rather than as local MarketingStatus findings.
The set of resources using `MarketingStatus` differs between R4 and R6. This report does not assess resource-level element paths, cardinalities, or search parameters for those containing resources.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 differential narrative or change log for `MarketingStatus` was available in the supplied local inputs. The analysis is based on direct StructureDefinition comparison.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official HL7 diff/change-note page explaining the R6 cardinality and wording changes would improve confidence in the justification and intended migration strategy.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Full human-authored R4 and R6 specification pages were not compared; only the StructureDefinitions and embedded generated R6 narrative were inspected.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Comparing the published datatype pages and ballot notes could confirm whether the shortened computable definitions are accompanied by additional explanatory guidance elsewhere.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The core datatype has no local terminology bindings, so no expansion comparison was performed. External profiles may bind `country`, `jurisdiction`, or `status` more tightly than the core datatype.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Profile-specific ValueSets, CodeSystems, and expansions would be needed to assess implementation-specific terminology breaks.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is `6.0.0-ballot4`, not a final normative release package. Ballot content can change before publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the comparison against the final R6 package when it is published.
